title: Apply to register as a silent elector
summary: You can apply to be registered as a silent elector if you believe that having your address on the publicly available electoral roll puts you or your family’s safety at risk.
intro:
If you believe that having your address on the publicly available electoral roll could put you or your family’s safety at risk, you can apply to be registered as a silent elector.

This means your address will not be shown on future electoral rolls.

Only your name and electoral division will appear.

If you need a paper form, contact the AEC.

Your application for silent elector status must explain in detail what you consider the risk to be and why your, or your family’s, personal safety is at risk.

The Divisional Returning Officer will notify you of the decision in writing. The information in your application will remain strictly confidential.

To stop the address from being associated with your surname on the electoral roll, family members with the same surname enrolled at your address should also consider becoming silent electors.

They must submit their own application for silent registration and can request silent status on the grounds that you have it.
who_can_apply: You must believe that having your address on the publicly available electoral roll could put you or your family’s safety at risk.

If you need a paper form, contact the AEC.
Family members with the same surname enrolled at your address must submit their own application for silent registration and can request silent status on the grounds that you have it.
